name: James 'Sonny' Crockett
summary: A vice detective who has spent six weeks living as Jimmy Burnett, a Fort Lauderdale boat dealer with money and no fixed address. The cover has started to fit better than the badge.
look: Sandy hair, three days of stubble, pale stone linen jacket over a white T-shirt, no socks, loafers, one gold chain.
continuity: From scene 32 onward Crockett is seen through Burnett's wardrobe: linen, loafers, a cigarette case. The badge only exists off-frame. In the warehouse (scene 68) he stops being Burnett; after that he wears his own clothes, and by the marina (scene 86) the passport goes in the water.

name: Ricardo Tubbs
summary: A former NYPD detective who came south for a revenge that never paid out. He is the one who counts the cost of a case on the people standing next to it.
look: Black, close-cropped, charcoal suit with the collar open, thin gold chain, a stillness he uses like a weapon.
continuity: Carries Eddie Marin's watch from scene 22 to scene 85, when he gives it to Lupe. At the causeway (scene 73) he has the shot on a man who has a child in the car and does not take it.

name: Lt. Martin Castillo
summary: The lieutenant who says the least and sees the most. He sends people into rooms he cannot watch and then waits up for them.
look: Mexican-American, dark hair swept straight back, dark suit, black tie, black shirt, a face that does nothing until it has decided.
continuity: Never raises his voice. Stands at windows with the blinds open. In scene 88 he is alone on a roof with the ledgers; that is the only time we see him off the clock.

name: Gina Calabrese
summary: Undercover officer who goes into the Hands of the Gulf thrift chain as a volunteer and finds out what moves at three in the morning.
look: Dark shoulder-length hair, a small scar at the jaw, black leather jacket over a pale silk top, gold hoops.
continuity: Wears a volunteer's smock in scenes 15, 16 and 39. In scene 56 she is at the Miramar in a borrowed dress; the dress is torn by scene 60 and she is on a sling and a telephone by scene 87.

name: Trudy Joplin
summary: The squad's nerve centre: she reads the donations database, the manifests and the wire traffic, and she is usually the first to notice the thing everybody else walked past.
look: Close-cropped hair, gold hoops, pale coral suit with the jacket pushed back, reading glasses she hates.
continuity: At the boards from scene 3 onward. In scene 43 she finds Eddie Marin's eleven-dollar donation envelope; in scene 87 she types the seventy-one page report.

name: Stan Switek
summary: A surveillance man with a gambling habit and eight months of small betrayals behind him. He is not a bad policeman; he is a man who kept borrowing from tomorrow.
look: Heavy, moustache, thinning hair, turquoise and cream printed shirt, sweating through it by noon.
continuity: Sweats through every scene from 11 on. Takes half the buy money back in scene 30. Wears a wire in scene 54 when he is already compromised, and loses the badge in scene 79.

name: Larry Zito
summary: Switek's partner and the quiet half of the van. He covers for Switek longer than he should and then does the one thing that saves him.
look: Lean, dark hair, grey-brown suit with the tie loosened, a face built for sitting in a parked car.
continuity: Bandaged shoulder from scene 55; he is in the warehouse anyway in scene 66. He is the one who finds the bet slips in scene 46 and says nothing until scene 53.

name: Izzy Moreno
summary: A man who knows every warehouse, truck and bank in Miami and will trade any of them for a favour. He is funny on purpose, which is how he survives.
look: Loud rayon shirt worn open, heavy gold chain, trimmed moustache, an unlit cigar he is always about to smoke.
continuity: Only ever meets Crockett in Little Havana or at his lot, never at OCB. The cigar is never lit. In scene 80 he drives the donation truck into the warehouse.

name: Marta Escobar
role: Director, Hands of the Gulf relief charity
summary: Runs sixteen thrift stores, a warehouse and a relief pipeline to three countries, and has photographs with governors and a bishop. She built a laundering route that pays for itself in donated bandages.
look: Cream linen suit, pearls, careful hair, the warm authority of a woman who has never been refused a table.
continuity: Touches people exactly once, in scene 20, and it matters. Arrested at her own desk in scene 81; she asks for a lawyer and mentions the bishop.

name: Ray Coburn
summary: A burnt-out federal agent running a witness inside a drug pipeline by letting half the drugs through. He is right about the arithmetic and wrong about everything else.
look: Grey stubble, a suit he has slept in, coffee he has reheated, the eyes of a man who stopped going home.
continuity: Never stands when visitors come in. Takes the ledger in scene 67, puts a twelve-year-old in his car in scene 71, and signs a deal in scene 82.
